headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 9 studies yielded an overall effect size of 1.3 (95% CI: 1.11–1.53), suggesting that red meat is associated with a higher risk of bladder cancer. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was very high between-study heterogeneity (I² = 75.60%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.

sample_size.excerpt: We prospectively followed 82,002 Swedish women and men who were free from cancer and completed a food-frequency questionnaire in 1997. Incident cases of bladder cancer were identified in the Swedish cancer registries.

cases.excerpt: During a mean follow-up of 9.4 years, 485 incident cases of bladder cancer (76 women and 409 men) were ascertained in the cohort.

effect_size.excerpt: We observed no association between the intake of total or any specific type of meat and the risk of bladder cancer. extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: In a cohort of 101,721 subjects in the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening Trial, we analyzed the association of processed meat intake with bladder cancer risk. After a median of 12.5 years of follow-up, 776 new cases of bladder cancer were identified.

studies.Title: Dietary consumption and diet diversity and risk of developing bladder cancer: results from the South and East China case-control study.
studies.Reference: Dietary consumption and diet diversity and risk of developing bladder cancer: results from the South and East China case-control study.
studies.Population: Chinese patients and controls from four hospitals
studies.comparison_type: Highest versus lowest level of red meat consumption

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: A case-control study of 487 cases and 469 controls was conducted in four hospitals in China.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: A case-control study of 487 cases and 469 controls was conducted in four hospitals in China.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The ORs of bladder cancer for red meat (OR = 1.8, 95 % CI:1.1-3.0;p(trend) = 0.01), organ meat (OR = 1.6, 95 % CI:0.9-2.9;p(trend) = 0.04), leafy vegetables (OR = 2.9, 95 % CI:1.6-5.4;p trend = 0.003), bulb vegetables (OR = 2.3, 95 % CI:1.3-4.0;p(trend) = 0.003), and preserved vegetables (OR = 2.3, 95 % CI:1.2-4.2;p(trend) = 0.02) were significantly increased when comparing the highest to lowest level of consumption.
